mechanism_narrative: A lower current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return for SPX when FEDFUNDS is in the bottom 25% of its historical distribution is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising FEDFUNDS and rising UNRATE indicates a tightening monetary policy coinciding with labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect (FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE rising) fails to predict negative returns: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market expansion regime (HOUST above 2000 thousand units), rising home construction activity signals strong consumer demand and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST exceeds 2000 thousand units.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A higher current level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) reflects a robust labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return for SPX when PAYEMS is in the top 25% of its historical distribution is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates broad-based economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO rise in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply contraction regime (INDPRO below 100), a decline in industrial production signals manufacturing weakness, reducing corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO falls below 100.
